entry.title: Analysis of Apple's On-Device Personal Knowledge Graph and macOS Daemons
entry.content:
Links: 8rank.ai | hacker news

Apple’s macOS features background daemons like knowledgeconstructiond and intelligenceplatformd that automatically construct an on-device personal knowledge graph. The system cross-references local data sources—including contacts, calendar events, photos, messages, location signals, and device activity—to build a queryable repository of user relationships and behaviors.

Security researchers at Eighth Rank analyzed the underlying SQLite databases within the IntelligencePlatform directory, detailing the structure's entity classes and relationship predicates. To help users inspect what data is stored locally, the researchers also released an open-source tool called iKnow while highlighting potential privacy and security implications associated with comprehensive on-device data aggregation.

entry.title: PWN Research Details Firecracker MicroVM Escape and Host Root Execution
entry.content:
Links: pwn.ai | hacker news

PWN Research published a technical write-up detailing a complete escape from an AWS Firecracker microVM (version 1.16.1), demonstrating how a guest can achieve root code execution on the host. By leveraging a previously established host memory access primitive, the technique identifies the Firecracker virtual machine monitor process, maps its virtual memory under ASLR, and locates the active vCPU thread's saved register frame.

The exploit intercepts the return from the KVM ioctl by modifying the saved instruction pointer and stack frame to execute custom host commands before seamlessly resuming normal operation. This compromise preserves guest responsiveness and process stability while highlighting critical security boundaries in container and microVM virtualization setups.

entry.title: Internet-wide Scan Finds Services Listening on TCP Port 0
entry.content:
Links: acid.vegas | lobsters | hacker news

An internet-wide scan of IPv4 addresses for open TCP port 0 identified over one million responding hosts. While port 0 is a reserved value typically used by operating systems to assign ephemeral ports, raw-packet scanning tools can bypass kernel-level restrictions to detect active responses.

Findings included standard protocols like SSH, MySQL, and HTTP, as well as specialized industrial and building automation equipment such as Beckhoff PLCs, Gira HomeServers, and Trane Tracer Synchrony controllers. A high percentage of responding addresses were F5 BIG-IP load balancers.

entry.title: SourceHut meta.sr.ht Registration Bypass Vulnerability (CVE-2026-121728)
entry.content:
Links: blog.arusekk.pl | lobsters

A logic error in the SourceHut `meta.sr.ht` platform allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass disabled registration settings. The vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-121728, occurs because the GraphQL backend's `/register/step2` endpoint fails to verify if registration is enabled, even when the frontend indicates that registration is closed. Attackers can bypass the restriction by using a CSRF token obtained from the `/login` endpoint.

The flaw was introduced during an architectural migration from Flask to a Go-based GraphQL backend, where the registration verification was omitted in the new implementation. The vulnerability affects versions 0.56.11 through 0.88.9. A fix has been released following the researcher's disclosure in November 2026.

entry.title: OpenSSH on musl-based Linux Distributions Vulnerable to Password Bypass
entry.content:
Links: sshhole.com | hacker news

OpenSSH installations running on musl libc—including Alpine, OpenWrt, and Buildroot—are vulnerable to a password bypass affecting accounts with no password (marked with '*' in /etc/shadow). When a password longer than 256 characters is provided, musl's crypt() function returns '*' due to a length limit in its SHA512 implementation, which OpenSSH incorrectly validates as a successful match.

The vulnerability specifically affects systems using musl that do not utilize PAM and have password authentication enabled. To mitigate this risk, users are advised to upgrade to OpenSSH 10.6p2 or disable password authentication in their SSH configuration.

entry.title: Steal My Bitcoin Experiment Tests PHP2Shell Exploitability
entry.content:
Links: pavursec.com | lobsters | hacker news

The PHP2Shell vulnerability was tested through the "Steal My Bitcoin" experiment to determine if it was exploitable in a live environment and if AI could assist unskilled attackers. The challenge used a PHP website hosting a $500 bitcoin wallet and a binary that outputs the wallet's private key upon successful exploitation. Although one participant successfully exploited the server, the experiment found that unskilled attackers using AI were largely unsuccessful.

The experiment attracted approximately 120,000 unique visitors and generated 13 million HTTP requests. Out of 20,000 substantive attempts, only one participant successfully exfiltrated data. These results suggest that while the vulnerability is practical to exploit, the technical complexity of the attack limits success among non-experts, despite reports of its potential for widespread exploitation.
